newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUG 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Geelong Australian Football League captain Barry Stoneham has been suspended for three matches by the Australian Football League Tribunal. Stoneham pleaded guilty for misconduct after he was reported on video evidence by a field umpire for striking Essendon player Michael Symons. Page 36.

The Sydney Swans Australian Football League club said charges against player Tony Lockett relating to an alleged greyhound scam will be dropped. The Sydney full-forward was to appear in court today to face charges of theft and false accounting. age 36.

Australian swimmer Grant Hackett has claimed Australia its tenth gold medal at the Pan Pacific swimming championships. Hackett won gold in the 1500-metres freestyle, despite suffering a debilitating virus. Page 36.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian swimmer Samantha Riley failed to beat the world record in the 200-metres breaststroke by half a second at the Pan Pacific swimming championships last night. Riley's swim has been recorded as the world's seconded-fastest this year, and gave her a second gold medal for the meet. Page 48.

Australian Rugby League clubs remain sceptical at an offer by News Ltd to fund 14 clubs at a reported price of A$4.5 million-a-year, or A$350 million over five years. The offer is A$1 million is excess of what ARL clubs already receive from Optus, and would require six clubs to be cut. Page 48.

Racing car driver Peter Brock has confirmed he will race at the Bathurst 1000 in October this year for the last time, despite opposition from his own Holden racing team. This year's race will be Brock's 29th start, and his last, as the racing legend inteds to retire. Page 46.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League Commission will meet today to finalise a decision over television rights and the Docklands Stadium. It is expected the successful television bidder will sell parts of the football coverage to other networks, with the potential for five games to be telecast live every week. Page C20.

Australian swimmer Matt Dunn has won his second gold medal at the Pan Pacific games in Japan after winning the 200-metres individual medley. The Sydney swimmer improved upon his previous time from the Atlanta Olympics by a fraction of a second. Page C20

The New Zealand All Black rugby union team has announced one change to its lineup for the Tri-Nations Test against Australia in Dunedin. Glen Osborne will replace winger Tana Umaga for the game on Saturday. Page C19.
THE HERALD SUN

Collingwood Australian Football League player Damian Monkhorst has been warned his contract with the club will not be renewed unless he reaches a suitable fitness level. Monkhorst has been informed he must lose 10 kilograms to ensure that his contract is renewed. Page 96.

Melbourne Australian Football League club chief executive Cameron Schwab has confirmed Sydney Swans assistant coach Damian Drum is on the shortlist of candidates for Melbourne's coaching job next year. Other candidates vying for the coaching position incude Greg Hutchison, Neale Daniher and Peter Schwab. Page 94.

Tasmanian cyclist Matthew Atkins won the Tour of the Grampians yesterday, despite suffering a heavy cold. Atkins finished the 125-kilometre race in just over three hours, securing himself a place in the Vic-Health Herald Sun Tour next month. Page 90.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

A leading New Zealand sports radio talkback host says the Australian rugby union team cannot win in this Saturday's Tri-Nations Test against the New Zealand All Blacks. Murray Deaker says Australia has never won a game in Dunedin, and the temperature and crowd factor will work against the Wallabies. Page 87.

Horse trainer Rick Hore-Lacy and owner Peter Woodard will today assess whether the Group 1 Manikato Stakes favourite Spartacus will run in Sydney or Melbourne on Saturday. Spartacus has also been entered in the Group 3 Premier Stakes at Rosehill Gardens a a precautionary measure. Page 88.

The Penrith Panthers women's netball team have lost their chance of gaining a spot in the Dairy Farmers State League playoffs after losing 49-67 to Bankstown in Sydney. Semi-finals of the State League are scheduled to be played on August 27. Page 88.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
